answer_summary: The independently derived Process B steady state is [HBrO2]_B = 5.04e-11 M and the switching condition gives [Br-]_critical = 3.00e-7 M. The slow bromide decay has kappa = 2 k4 [HBrO2]_B [H+] = 0.16128 s^-1, so tau = ln((7.0e-4)/(3.00e-7))/kappa = 48.0844068661... s, reported as 48.1 s to three significant figures.
assumptions: The printed elementary reactions obey mass-action rate laws.
The HBrO2 and BrO2 radical concentrations use the steady-state approximation requested in T2-A2, with physically positive concentrations when cancellation is used.
The almost-immediate return from critical to maximum bromide has negligible duration compared with the slow Process B branch, exactly as directed by the T2-A5 source text.

On the long colourless Process B branch, Ce(IV) is negligible because the source attributes that state to Ce(III); hence the Ce(IV)-dependent Process C rate is confined to the rapid regeneration transient for the period approximation.
Printed constants are treated as exact according to TASK.json; the final answer uses its predeclared three-significant-figure reporting policy.
